doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Tulsa, Ernie Fields and Melvin Moore
summary: Woods and Tate talk about the Tulsa feel, Ernie Fields, Bostic and singer Melvin Moore.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: You know I spent some time in that area myself, when you talk about Tulsa, Oklahoma, I spent ten years in Tulsa. And I noticed that the feel is different. It’s more relaxed, it’s got a nice bounce to it, but it doesn’t sound so jumpy and hurried. And it’s still kind of like that.
Did you know — you know Ernie Fields then? I’m sure you know him.

Yeah. Fields, and Bostic, I think Bostic was from Tulsa. I hired Bostic in the T. Holder band. He was ahead of his time. He was some saxophone player. And who else? I think Little Ernie, I think somebody told me Ernie was still living.
Well I left in ‘90 and he was still living.
Yeah, I heard he was — how long ago was this?

Yeah, I heard he was. Melvin Moore told me this. Did you know a singer by the name of Melvin Moore? He used to sing with Ernie Fields for a long time, and Don Albert out of San Antonio. And I think he told me that Ernie’s still going, still around, with us.
